{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# exp-012: GSM8K Pilot - Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct
# 30 problems, K=12, T=0.7, math domain validation
# ~1h GPU
# Purpose: validate SICA on standard math reasoning benchmark (numerical answers)
set -e
cd /root/symb_invariant_consensus
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct"
PORT=8000
RESULTS_DIR="results/exp012_gsm8k"
mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"

# Check if port is already in use
if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: Port $PORT is already in use. Another vLLM instance may be running."
    echo "Please wait for it to finish or manually stop it before running this script."
    exit 1
fi

# Start vLLM
echo "=== [$(date)] Starting vLLM (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct) on port $PORT ==="
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --max-model-len 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --port $PORT \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype auto > /tmp/vllm_exp012.log 2>&1 &
VLLM_PID=$!
echo "vLLM PID: $VLLM_PID"

# Wait for vLLM ready (up to 300s)
echo "Waiting for vLLM to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
    if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "vLLM ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: vLLM process died. Check /tmp/vllm_exp012.log"
        tail -20 /tmp/vllm_exp012.log
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if ! curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: vLLM did not start within 300s"
    kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

# Run GSM8K pilot
echo "=== [$(date)] Running GSM8K pilot: K=12, T=0.7, 30 problems ==="
python3 scripts/run_gsm8k_pilot.py \
    --mode vllm \
    --k 12 \
    --n-problems 30 \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --max-tokens 4096 \
    --api-base "http://localhost:$PORT/v1" \
    --model auto \
    --seed 42 \
    --data-path data/gsm8k_200.json \
    --output "$RESULTS_DIR/exp012_gsm8k_results.json" \
    --save-intermediates

# Cleanup
echo "=== [$(date)] Stopping vLLM ==="
kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "EXP012_DONE"

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# exp-004: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct scaling validation on D012
# 30 FOLIO + 30 ProofWriter, K=12, T=0.7
# ~2h GPU
# Purpose: smaller model scaling point for C0 gradient claim
#
# NOTE: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct must be downloaded first.
# If model is not present, this script will download it via modelscope.
set -e
cd /root/symb_invariant_consensus
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct"
PORT=8000
RESULTS_DIR="results/exp004_qwen7b"
mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"

# Check if model exists, download if not
if [ ! -d "$MODEL" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A $MODEL 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    echo "=== [$(date)] Model not found. Downloading Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via modelscope ==="
    pip install modelscope -q 2>/dev/null
    python -c "
from modelscope import snapshot_download
snapshot_download('Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct', cache_dir='/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct')
"
    # Find the actual model path after download
    ACTUAL_PATH=$(find /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct -name "config.json" -type f | head -1 | xargs dirname)
    if [ -z "$ACTUAL_PATH" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Model download failed or config.json not found"
        exit 1
    fi
    MODEL="$ACTUAL_PATH"
    echo "Model downloaded to: $MODEL"
else
    # Check for nested modelscope structure
    NESTED=$(find "$MODEL" -name "config.json" -type f | head -1 | xargs dirname 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$NESTED" ] && [ "$NESTED" != "$MODEL" ]; then
        MODEL="$NESTED"
    fi
fi

echo "Using model path: $MODEL"

# Check if port is already in use
if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: Port $PORT is already in use. Another vLLM instance may be running."
    echo "Please wait for it to finish or manually stop it before running this script."
    exit 1
fi

# Start vLLM
echo "=== [$(date)] Starting vLLM (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) on port $PORT ==="
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --port $PORT \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype auto > /tmp/vllm_exp004.log 2>&1 &
VLLM_PID=$!
echo "vLLM PID: $VLLM_PID"

# Wait for vLLM ready (up to 180s for 7B model)
echo "Waiting for vLLM to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 180); do
    if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "vLLM ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: vLLM process died. Check /tmp/vllm_exp004.log"
        tail -20 /tmp/vllm_exp004.log
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if ! curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: vLLM did not start within 180s"
    kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

# Run SICA pipeline
echo "=== [$(date)] Running SICA pipeline: K=12, T=0.7, 60 problems ==="
python3 run_full_mvp.py \
    --mode vllm \
    --k 12 \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --max-tokens 4096 \
    --api-base "http://localhost:$PORT/v1" \
    --math-data data/empty.json \
    --pw-data data/proofwriter_30.json \
    --folio-data data/folio_30.json \
    --output "$RESULTS_DIR/exp004_qwen7b_results.json" \
    --save-intermediates \
    --seed 42

# Cleanup
echo "=== [$(date)] Stopping vLLM ==="
kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "EXP004_DONE"

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on StrategyQA (cross-model cross-domain validation)
# 60 problems, K=12, T=0.7
# ~1.5h GPU
# Purpose: eliminate model-specific concerns, Mistral on commonsense reasoning
set -e
cd /root/symb_invariant_consensus
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/models/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3"
PORT=8000
RESULTS_DIR="results/mistral_strategyqa"
mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"

# Check if port is already in use
if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: Port $PORT is already in use. Another vLLM instance may be running."
    echo "Please wait for it to finish or manually stop it before running this script."
    exit 1
fi

# Start vLLM
echo "=== [$(date)] Starting vLLM (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3) on port $PORT ==="
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --port $PORT \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype auto > /tmp/vllm_mistral_strategyqa.log 2>&1 &
VLLM_PID=$!
echo "vLLM PID: $VLLM_PID"

# Wait for vLLM ready (up to 180s)
echo "Waiting for vLLM to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 180); do
    if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "vLLM ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: vLLM process died. Check /tmp/vllm_mistral_strategyqa.log"
        tail -20 /tmp/vllm_mistral_strategyqa.log
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if ! curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: vLLM did not start within 180s"
    kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

# Run StrategyQA evaluation
echo "=== [$(date)] Running StrategyQA: Mistral-7B, K=12, T=0.7, 60 problems ==="
python3 scripts/eval_strategyqa.py \
    --mode vllm \
    --k 12 \
    --n-problems 60 \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --max-tokens 2048 \
    --api-base "http://localhost:$PORT/v1" \
    --model auto \
    --seed 42 \
    --data data/strategyqa_200.json \
    --output "$RESULTS_DIR/mistral_strategyqa_results.json" \
    --save-intermediates

# Cleanup
echo "=== [$(date)] Stopping vLLM ==="
kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "MISTRAL_STRATEGYQA_DONE"

High C0 produces abundant constraints, but these constraints fail to distinguish correct from incorrect answers, reducing MAX-SAT to counting. Validated across 3 reasoning domains × 4 instruction-scale model families + 1 full reasoning model (QwQ-32B). [Scope: this finding characterizes same-model self-extraction pipelines; methods using external verifiers or trained extractors may not share this limitation.]\\n2. **Operating Regime is Empirically Empty**: Five model families confirm SICA provides no accuracy gain over majority voting: (a) Qwen-14B n=804 Δ=+0.25pp n.s., (b) Mistral-7B n=60 Δ=0.0pp exact, (c) LLaMA-8B StrategyQA n=200 Δ=+2.0pp p=0.424, (d) LLaMA-8B FOLIO n=204 Δ=-2.4pp, (e) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B n=60 Δ=-3.3pp. Full reasoning model QwQ-32B shows near-zero diversity (C0<5%), making SICA degenerate to SC. Instruction-scale models (including distilled reasoning models) show high diversity (C0=38-62%) but constraints lack discriminative power. No tested condition achieves both requirements simultaneously.\\n3. **C0 as Necessary-but-Insufficient Diagnostic**: C0 reliably predicts when symbolic consensus CANNOT help (C0<5% → method degenerates to SC), but high C0 does NOT guarantee gains. C0 is a zero-cost early stopping criterion for practitioners considering symbolic aggregation methods.\\n\\n## Core Insight\\nLLM self-extracted FOL constraints don't improve majority voting because of a **capability trap**: the method needs output diversity (disagreement to resolve) AND discriminative constraints (to resolve it correctly). While instruction-scale models produce abundant diversity (C0=38-62%) and constraints, these self-extracted constraints lack the discriminative power to distinguish correct from incorrect answers (precision ~0.50, no better than chance). MAX-SAT optimization over such non-discriminative constraints degenerates to counting, performing no better than simple majority voting. We provide the first systematic empirical study characterizing this failure mode across 3 reasoning domains, 4 instruction-scale model families, and 1 full reasoning model. [Positioning: Logic-LM and LINC documented that LLM-to-FOL translation is error-prone; our contribution is systematic quantification at per-problem granularity (n=307) showing constraints are non-discriminative, the constraint ablation proving MAX-SAT adds nothing beyond counting, and C0 as a deployment diagnostic.]\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n- **Problem**: Recent work proposes augmenting LLM reasoning with symbolic methods, extracting formal constraints from reasoning traces and using solvers for answer selection. But when should practitioners invest in such methods vs. simple majority voting?\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: SC (Wang et al. 2023), USC (Chen et al. 2023), Logic-LM (Pan et al. 2023), LINC (Olausson et al. 2023), ORM/PRM (Cobbe et al. 2021, Lightman et al. 2023), Weighted SC (Taubenfeld et al. 2024). None systematically characterize when symbolic aggregation helps vs. when it degenerates to voting.\\n- **Our framing**: We instantiate symbolic consensus as SICA (MAX-SAT over extracted FOL constraints) and systematically evaluate across 3 domains × 4 instruction-scale model families + 1 full reasoning model. We find SICA ≈ SC everywhere, and identify a structural reason: the **capability trap**.\\n- **Headline result**: \\\"Across 3 reasoning domains and 5 models spanning instruction, distilled-reasoning, and full-reasoning architectures, SICA provides no significant accuracy gain over SC. Five models (combined N>1,300) show Δ ranging from -3.3pp to +2.0pp, none significant. The constraint ablation reveals MAX-SAT ≈ count-only ≈ random-weight. ## ROADMAP 审查 — D037 Dream审稿反馈处理

**结论**: WARNING

### 正面评价

- [severity: info] **Framing 缩窄正确**：标题和 Claims 从"symbolic consensus"缩窄到"self-extracted constraints"，与实证证据范围匹配。Concern #14 明确承认 DyLoS/Aristotle/FoVer 等方法在同类 benchmark 上有效——这是对审稿人攻击的预防性防御。

- [severity: info] **Citation 要求具体化**：30+ 引用的分类清单（SC 系列、neuro-symbolic、TTS、verification、negative results）是 EMNLP 的合理门槛。Required Citations 列表可直接指导 Paper Agent。

- [severity: info] **Claim Scoping Rules 合理**：n=60 = "suggestive"，n≥200 = "confirming"。Combined N>1,300 的统计说法要求注明 804/1300 来自 Qwen-14B 单条件——这是诚实的 framing。

### 需要关注的问题

- [severity: warning] **Oracle extraction 实验设计非 trivial，需在编码前明确方案**：FOLIO 的 gold FOL 是每题的逻辑公理/规则集（per-problem），不是 per-trace 约束。SICA pipeline 从每条 trace 提取约束，然后跨 trace 聚合。将 gold FOL 接入 MAX-SAT 有多种方式，语义差异大：(a) 用 gold FOL 替代所有 trace 的 extracted constraints → 所有 trace 共享同一 constraint set，MAX-SAT 退化为 deterministic；(b) 用 gold FOL 验证每条 trace 的推理过程是否逻辑一致 → 这是 Logic-LM 而非 SICA；(c) 用 gold FOL + 每条 trace 的最终答案做 satisfiability check → 需定义 answer 如何映射到 FOL satisfiability。建议 Agent 在编码前先写 1 页实验设计文档，明确 input/output/evaluation protocol，避免实验结果不可解读。

- [severity: warning] **Claim 3 C0 gradient risk 仍未解决**：当前 C0 只有两个聚类（QwQ-32B <5% vs instruction models 38-62%），无中间梯度。温度消融是关键机会——如果 T=0.3 给出 C0≈15-25%，则形成 3 级梯度；如果仍然聚类在 <5% 或 >35%，需将 Claim 3 从"gradient diagnostic"降级为"binary indicator"。建议温度实验完成后立即评估 C0 分布，作为 Claim 3 措辞的决策依据。

- [severity: info] **Concern #15（MAX-SAT ≈ weighted voting?）是论文定位的关键问题**：paper_framing 正确标注了这一点。建议 Paper Agent 写 Method section 时，必须用公式明确展示 SICA 的 MAX-SAT 是否做 cross-answer evaluation（约束 c_i 是否同时对多个候选答案求值），还是只在每个答案的 trace 内部求解。如果是后者，审稿人会直接指出"这就是 weighted voting with extra steps"。

- [severity: info] **Re-dream 不应阻塞 Paper Agent 全部工作**：Method、Related Work、Experiment Setup 等章节不依赖 dream 分数验证。建议 Paper Agent 先写这些章节，re-dream 并行跑，结果回来后再写 Abstract/Introduction/Conclusion。

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'legend.fontsize': 8,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.05,
})

OUT = '/root/symb_invariant_consensus/artifacts/figures'

CB_BLUE = '#0173B2'
CB_ORANGE = '#DE8F05'
CB_GREEN = '#029E73'
CB_RED = '#D55E00'
CB_PURPLE = '#CC78BC'
CB_GRAY = '#949494'

# ============================================================
# F2: Per-problem Constraint Analysis Scatter Plot
# ============================================================
df = pd.read_csv('/root/symb_invariant_consensus/analysis/f2_per_problem.csv')

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.0))

dataset_colors = {'proofwriter': CB_BLUE, 'folio': CB_ORANGE}

no_flip = df[df['sica_flipped'] == 0]
flipped = df[df['sica_flipped'] == 1]

correct_flip = flipped[(flipped['sica_correct'] == 1) & (flipped['sc_correct'] == 0)]
wrong_flip = flipped[flipped['sica_correct'] == 0]
neutral_flip = flipped[(flipped['sica_correct'] == 1) & (flipped['sc_correct'] == 1)]

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

def jx(n): return rng.normal(0, 0.012, n)
def jy(n): return rng.normal(0, 0.002, n)

for ds, color in dataset_colors.items():
    mask = no_flip['dataset'] == ds
    sub = no_flip[mask]
    ax.scatter(sub['vote_entropy'] + jx(len(sub)),
               sub['constraint_exclusion_rate'] + jy(len(sub)),
               c=color, marker='o', s=20, alpha=0.25, edgecolors='none', zorder=2)

for ds, color in dataset_colors.items():
    mask = correct_flip['dataset'] == ds
    sub = correct_flip[mask]
    ax.scatter(sub['vote_entropy'] + jx(len(sub)),
               sub['constraint_exclusion_rate'] + jy(len(sub)),
               c=color, marker='*', s=80, alpha=0.9, edgecolors='k',
               linewidths=0.3, zorder=4)

for ds, color in dataset_colors.items():
    mask = wrong_flip['dataset'] == ds
    sub = wrong_flip[mask]
    ax.scatter(sub['vote_entropy'] + jx(len(sub)),
               sub['constraint_exclusion_rate'] + jy(len(sub)),
               c=color, marker='X', s=50, alpha=0.85, edgecolors='k',
               linewidths=0.3, zorder=4)

for ds, color in dataset_colors.items():
    mask = neutral_flip['dataset'] == ds
    sub = neutral_flip[mask]
    ax.scatter(sub['vote_entropy'] + jx(len(sub)),
               sub['constraint_exclusion_rate'] + jy(len(sub)),
               c=color, marker='D', s=30, alpha=0.7, edgecolors='k',
               linewidths=0.3, zorder=3)

ax.set_xlabel('Vote Entropy')
ax.set_ylabel('Constraint Exclusion Rate')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=CB_BLUE, label='ProofWriter'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=CB_ORANGE, label='FOLIO'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor=CB_GRAY,
           markersize=6, alpha=0.5, label='No flip'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='*', color='w', markerfacecolor=CB_GRAY,
           markeredgecolor='k', markeredgewidth=0.3,
           markersize=10, label='Correct flip'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='X', color='w', markerfacecolor=CB_GRAY,
           markeredgecolor='k', markeredgewidth=0.3,
           markersize=7, label='Wrong flip'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='D', color='w', markerfacecolor=CB_GRAY,
           markeredgecolor='k', markeredgewidth=0.3,
           markersize=6, label='Neutral flip'),
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9,
          edgecolor='#cccccc', ncol=2)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f'{OUT}/f2_per_problem_scatter.pdf')
fig.savefig(f'{OUT}/f2_per_problem_scatter.png', dpi=300)
plt.close(fig)
print(f'F2 saved. Counts: no_flip={len(no_flip)}, correct_flip={len(correct_flip)}, wrong_flip={len(wrong_flip)}, neutral_flip={len(neutral_flip)}')

# ============================================================
# F4: C0 vs SICA-SC Gap
# ============================================================

For the LLaMA-8B results, I'm noticing a potential issue: the D012 experiment was flagged in the registry as noise and explicitly marked not to cite as evidence. The LLaMA-8B result with n=30 shows a strong +6.67pp signal, but the paper explicitly warns against citing this as evidence since a larger replication (n=204) reversed it to -2.45pp. Including it without visual distinction could mislead readers. I need to either remove it, mark it distinctly with reduced visual weight, or add confidence intervals showing the uncertainty. The same problem exists with Qwen-14B's D012 subset—the n=60 sample inflates the effect compared to the larger n=804 dataset which showed only +0.3pp.

The scatter plot fundamentally needs confidence intervals or some way to weight points by sample size, since small-sample results look equally authoritative as large-sample ones despite their vastly different reliability. The framing says it should be C0 versus constraint precision at the experiment level, but the actual plot uses vote entropy versus constraint exclusion rate at the per-problem level. The per-problem version is actually stronger with more data points, but the axis labels need to align with the paper's description, so I should update the framing document to match the actual visualization.

The figures look good overall—no titles since captions go in LaTeX, Times New Roman serif font at appropriate sizes for EMNLP, and a colorblind-friendly palette. # Oracle Extraction Experiment Design

## 1. FOLIO Gold FOL Format

`data/folio_full.json` contains 204 problems. Each has structured fields with human-annotated FOL:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `premises` | list[str] | NL premise sentences |
| `conclusion` | str | NL conclusion sentence |
| `premises_fol` | list[str] | Per-premise FOL formulas (1:1 with `premises`) |
| `conclusion_fol` | str | FOL formula for the conclusion |
| `answer` | str | Gold label: True / False / Unknown |

FOL syntax uses Unicode quantifiers and connectives: `∀x`, `→`, `¬`, `∧`, `∨`, `⊕` (XOR), with `Predicate(entity)` notation.

**Example (folio_000):**
```
premises_fol:
  - ∀x (TalentShows(x) → Engaged(x))
  - ∀x (TalentShows(x) ∨ Inactive(x))
  - ∀x (Chaperone(x) → ¬Students(x))
  - ∀x (Inactive(x) → Chaperone(x))
  - ∀x (AcademicCareer(x) → Students(x))
  - (Engaged(bonnie) ∧ Students(bonnie)) ⊕ (¬Engaged(bonnie) ∧ ¬Students(bonnie))

conclusion_fol: Engaged(bonnie)
answer: Unknown
```

**Example (folio_003):**
```
premises_fol:
  - ∀x (Meeting(x) → AppearInCompany(x))
  - ∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → Meetings(x))
  - ∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x))
  - ∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → WorkRemotelyFromHome(x))
  - ∀x (InOtherCountries(x) → WorkRemotelyFromHome(x))
  - ∀x (Manager(x) → ¬WorkRemotelyFromHome(x))
  - Manager(james) ⊕ AppearInCompany(james)

conclusion_fol: LunchInCompany(james)
answer: Unknown
```

## 2. Three Oracle Schemes

### (a) Per-trace FOL Verification + MAX-SAT Aggregation

Each of k traces produces a candidate answer (True/False/Unknown). Gold FOL premises + conclusion are encoded into Z3. For each trace, check whether its candidate answer is logically consistent with the gold FOL:
- Answer "True" is consistent iff `premises ⊨ conclusion`
- Answer "False" is consistent iff `premises ⊨ ¬conclusion`
- Answer "Unknown" is consistent iff neither entailment holds

Each trace gets a binary consistency score (1 = consistent, 0 = inconsistent). MAX-SAT aggregation then selects the answer that maximizes total consistency-weighted support across traces.

- **Tests**: Whether constraint-based scoring with perfect constraints helps select better answers than raw majority vote.
- **Controls**: Extraction quality (replaced by gold FOL), isolating the aggregation mechanism.
- **SICA correspondence**: Replaces the "LLM constraint extraction" step; preserves per-trace scoring and MAX-SAT aggregation structure.
- **Answers core question**: Yes, directly. If gold-FOL+MAX-SAT > SC, aggregation adds value and the bottleneck is extraction. If gold-FOL+MAX-SAT = SC, aggregation itself is insufficient.

### (b) Shared Constraint Set (Direct FOL Solving)

Gold FOL premises + conclusion are fed to Z3 once to determine the correct label. All traces share this single oracle verdict.

- **Tests**: Whether gold FOL + Z3 can solve FOLIO (a prover ceiling, not an aggregation test).
- **Controls**: Everything (no LLM involved at inference).
- **SICA correspondence**: None. Eliminates both extraction AND aggregation. Changes SICA's core per-trace structure to a single global check.
- **Answers core question**: No. This bypasses aggregation entirely, so it cannot tell us whether aggregation adds value.

### (c) Per-trace Reasoning Chain Verification

Gold FOL is used to verify logical consistency of each trace's full reasoning chain (not just the final answer). Invalid traces are filtered before voting.

- **Tests**: Whether filtering logically invalid traces improves voting.
- **Controls**: Reasoning chain quality (verified by gold FOL).
- **SICA correspondence**: Closer to Logic-LM (single-trace verification) than SICA (cross-trace aggregation). Does not use MAX-SAT.
- **Answers core question**: Only partially. Tests trace filtering, not constraint aggregation.

## 3. Recommendation: Scheme (a)

Scheme (a) is the only design that isolates extraction quality while preserving SICA's aggregation mechanism. Scheme (b) solves the problem directly, bypassing aggregation entirely, making it useless for testing SICA's core claim. Scheme (c) tests trace filtering (a Logic-LM paradigm), not constraint aggregation (the SICA paradigm).

One subtlety: since gold FOL gives complete (not partial) constraints, scheme (a) provides an **upper bound** on what perfect extraction could achieve. Real extraction produces partial, noisy constraints, so oracle results represent the ceiling of the extraction-dependent pathway.

## 4. Input / Output / Evaluation Protocol

### Input
- **Gold FOL**: `data/folio_full.json` (fields: `premises_fol`, `conclusion_fol`, `answer`)
- **Trace data**: `results/exp020_folio_200/exp020_results.json` (k=12 traces per problem, n=204)
- Reuse exp020's existing traces and candidate answers; only replace the constraint extraction + scoring step

### Output Metrics
- Accuracy per method
- Delta (pp) between methods with 95% CI (bootstrap)
- McNemar's test p-value for pairwise significance

### Three-way Comparison

| Condition | Extraction | Aggregation | Source |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|--------|
| SC (baseline) | N/A | Majority vote | exp020 existing |
| SICA (self-extracted) | LLM | MAX-SAT | exp020 existing |
| Oracle-SICA | Gold FOL + Z3 | MAX-SAT | New experiment |

### Interpretation Framework

| Outcome | Interpretation | Implication |
|---------|---------------|-------------|
| Oracle-SICA > SC | Aggregation mechanism works; extraction quality is the bottleneck | Improve extraction (better prompts, specialized models, hybrid approaches) |
| Oracle-SICA ≈ SC | Even perfect constraints do not make MAX-SAT beat voting | Aggregation mechanism needs redesign or the problem class doesn't benefit from symbolic aggregation |
| Oracle-SICA < SC | Gold FOL integration with trace answers has implementation issues | Debug Z3 encoding or FOL parsing before drawing conclusions |
